target_claim: The proof's constructive induction defines a decomposition procedure (peel edges off E one at a time until an inclusion-minimal cut-subset F remains; split G-F into components A and B; partition E\F into E_A and E_B; recurse on G[A] and G[B]) whose output is claimed to express any cut E as a disjoint union of minimal cuts (bonds) OF G, via the lifting step at line 0051: 'a minimal cut in a subgraph like G[A] or G[B] is also a minimal cut in the entire graph G'.
failing_input: PRIMARY (a standard cut delta(S), where the theorem itself is TRUE): G = 4-cycle a-b-d-c-a, V={a,b,c,d}, E(G)={ab,ac,bd,cd}; S={b,c}; the cut E = delta(S) = {ab,ac,bd,cd} (all four edges). SECONDARY (solution's own definition of cut): G = K3 on {a,b,c}, E = {ab,bc,ca}. TERTIARY (triage pass-0 sketch): G = triangle abc plus pendant edge ad, E = {ad,ab}.
observed_vs_claimed: C4 instance: the procedure peels E to F={bd,cd} (a genuine bond, delta({d})), gets A={a,b,c}, B={d}, E_A={ab,ac}; inside G[A] (edges ab,ac only) it recurses and emits blocks {ac} and {ab}. Final output = {bd,cd} | {ac} | {ab}. Claimed: every emitted block is a minimal cut of G. Observed: C4 minus a single edge is still connected, so neither {ac} nor {ab} is a cut of G at all - the line-0051 lifting step is false, because the a-c reconnection through d was deleted along with F and returns in G. The brute-force oracle (exhaustive over all set partitions of E) shows a correct decomposition DOES exist here, namely delta({a})={ab,ac} and delta({d})={bd,cd}, so the procedure is unsound rather than the theorem being false. Section D of the test re-runs the procedure over all 10 admissible sequences of inclusion-minimal F-choices: none produces a partition of E into bonds of G, so the nondeterminism in 'choose one that is inclusion-wise minimal' does not rescue it. K3 instance: E={ab,bc,ca} is a cut under the solution's own definition (K3-E has 3 components > 1); the procedure outputs {ac,bc} | {ab} and {ab} is not a cut of K3; the oracle shows NO partition of E into bonds of K3 exists at all (bonds of K3 are exactly its three 2-edge subsets), so under the solution's own definition the statement it claims to prove is false. Pendant instance: the procedure aborts - with F={ad}, A={a,b,c}, E_A={ab}, and G[A]-{ab} (triangle minus one edge) is still connected, so line 0043's 'E_A is a cut in the subgraph G[A]' is false. Exhaustive census over all simple graphs on 3,4,5 labelled vertices and every cut E with |E|<=6: 37678 instances tested, 25727 refute the claim - 17209 abort at line 0043, 6914 emit a block that is not even a cut of G (line-0051 failure), 1604 abort at line 0025 ('removing F splits G into exactly two components' - observed 3 or 4). Restricted to connected G and standard cuts delta(S), where the theorem is unambiguously true: 11198 instances, 343 still counterexamples.
faithfulness_notes: The procedure is implemented exactly as written, bugs included: base case |E|=1 emits E; if E is inclusion-minimal, emit E; otherwise peel edges (deterministic sorted order) until an inclusion-minimal cut-subset F remains, take components of G-F, split E\F by component, recurse on the induced subgraphs. Peeling one edge at a time does reach an inclusion-minimal cut-subset because cut-ness is upward closed under enlarging the removal set, matching lines 0021-0022. Three steps the proof explicitly asserts are checked as assertions at the exact point of assertion and reported, never repaired: line 0025 (G-F has exactly two components), line 0031 (no edge of E\F crosses A-B), line 0043 (E_A is a cut of G[A]). Two charitable concessions were made, both of which can only help the solution: (1) when E_A or E_B is empty it is skipped as an empty union rather than flagged, even though the proof asserts both are cuts; (2) the F-choice is nondeterministic in the proof, so beyond the deterministic greedy run the test also enumerates every admissible inclusion-minimal F and confirms no choice yields a valid decomposition on the failing inputs. 'Cut' and 'minimal cut' are taken from the solution's own definitions at lines 0002-0005 (G-E has more components than G; no proper subset is a cut). All arithmetic is integer/set-theoretic - component counts via union-find, subset and set-partition enumeration - no floats anywhere, no sampling, no wall-clock timing; the run is fully deterministic. Nothing in the proof was unimplementable.
